name: PTC Inc.
key_signal: PTC trades 43% below its 52-week high and below both its 50- and 200-day moving averages, yet momentum has just turned positive (mom_21d +6.8%, MACD histogram +1.23) while trading at a forward PE of only 14.5x against 21.7% revenue growth and 34% ROE.
thesis: PTC's fundamentals remain best-in-class for application software: 84.7% gross margin, 41.6% operating margin, 21.7% revenue growth and a 33% FCF margin ($986M FCF on $3.0B revenue). The stock has been beaten down from $219.69 to $124.85 (a 43% drawdown) alongside broader software multiple compression, pushing the forward PE to just 14.5x for a company growing earnings and revenue at a double-digit clip — a PEG well below 1. Technicals are starting to inflect: 21-day momentum has turned positive (+6.8%) after a brutal 126-day slide (-25.2%), RSI is neutral at 50.8 rather than oversold-then-bounced, and the MACD histogram is solidly positive (+1.23), suggesting a bottoming process is underway even though price remains below both moving averages. With 20 analysts already rating this a 'buy' and a market cap of $14.4B, this is a liquid, well-scrutinized name where the recent momentum inflection combined with a genuinely cheap multiple relative to growth offers an attractive entry for a reversal trade.
bear_case: The technical picture is still structurally negative: price sits below both the 50-day ($130.4) and 200-day ($157.6) moving averages with no golden cross, and the 126-day momentum of -25% shows the primary trend remains down — a single month of bounce doesn't override a six-month downtrend, especially with 30-day annualized volatility near 49% meaning this 'bounce' could easily reverse just as fast. The trailing PE of 12x looks anomalously cheap next to a forward PE of 14.5x and an implausible reported earningsGrowth of 269%, strongly suggesting trailing earnings were inflated by a one-time gain (e.g., a divestiture) rather than reflecting sustainable earnings power — meaning the 'cheap' valuation is partly an illusion and the more honest forward multiple of 14.5x is much less of a bargain for a stock that's fallen 43% from its highs, often a sign the market is pricing in decelerating ARR/bookings growth in its core CAD/PLM franchise rather than a temporary dislocation.
